analysis:
Both changed files are CI test scripts: scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py (modified, lines 241-244) and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (added). They are not shipped provider runtime code. No change touches the provider WebSocket contract (TB-002), key custody (A-002/A-003), attestation (TB-009), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), or the fan helper (TB-010). The security-relevant content is what the tests pin about the CI routing design, and the tests only assert controls; they do not weaken them.

The test-ci-component-paths.py change only adjusts expectations: a `route` job needs `changes`, and the lane jobs need `[changes, route]`.

The route test asserts these properties of the router and its callers:
- The router workflow is workflow_call only, with `permissions: {}`, no secrets, no checkout and no id-token.
- The route step is hard-coded to https and verifies certificates. Plain HTTP and untrusted planes are never contacted.
- Fork PRs and pull_request_target never contact the plane.
- Only an exact label array for each profile is accepted. Anything else falls back to the Blacksmith label.
- Plane-supplied text cannot inject `::` workflow commands or markdown into stdout or the step summary.
- Replies are size-bounded, and the step is timeout-bounded and retries at most once on transient errors.
- Release, credentialed and signing workflows keep literal blacksmith runners and must not reference self-hosted labels or `needs.route`.
- Routed jobs must have read-only permissions, no secrets, no id-token, no environment, and a timeout of at most 60 minutes.

The test harness itself is safe. It strips host proxy and CA environment, uses a throwaway loopback TLS certificate, and refuses to hit the production plane when routing is on without a URL. Subprocess arguments are fixed, so there is no injection surface.

The residual point is outside the supplied evidence: the actual darkbloom-route.yml, the ci.yml wiring and the plane's own policy. These tests rely on them, and I could not verify them here. Self-hosted runners for PR jobs also carry a runner-isolation question. The test mitigates it by excluding forks, requiring read-only permissions and excluding secrets, but the runner hardening is not visible in this PR. No regression is identified in the supplied files.
